refs.quote: In adults and pediatric patients aged 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus, the recommended starting dosage of FARXIGA is 5 mg orally once daily to improve glycemic control. For additional glycemic control, the dosage can be increased to 10 mg orally once daily.

hepatic.value: No dose adjustment is recommended for patients with mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment; however, benefit-risk in severe hepatic impairment should be individually assessed since safety and efficacy have not been specifically studied in that population.

refs.quote: No dose adjustment is recommended for patients with mild, moderate, or severe hepatic impairment. However, the benefit-risk for the use of dapagliflozin in patients with severe hepatic impairment should be individually assessed since the safety and efficacy of dapagliflozin have not been specifically studied in this population [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.3) ] .
Dapagliflozin is an inhibitor of SGLT2. By inhibiting SGLT2, dapagliflozin reduces reabsorption of filtered glucose and thereby promotes urinary glucose excretion.

mg_safety.note: SGLT2 inhibitor; no neuromuscular junction blocking activity.

ng_tube.note: Film-coated 5 mg and 10 mg oral tablets; no specific enteral tube administration instructions in label.

mechanism_of_action.value: Selective inhibitor of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) in the proximal renal tubules, reducing reabsorption of filtered glucose and promoting urinary glucose excretion. Also reduces sodium reabsorption and increases distal sodium delivery, lowering cardiac preload/afterload and intraglomerular pressure via tubuloglomerular feedback.

refs.quote: By inhibiting SGLT2, dapagliflozin reduces reabsorption of filtered glucose and thereby promotes urinary glucose excretion. Dapagliflozin also reduces sodium reabsorption and increases the delivery of sodium to the distal tubule.
The metabolism of dapagliflozin is primarily mediated by UGT1A9; CYP-mediated metabolism is a minor clearance pathway in humans.
Dapagliflozin is a weak substrate of the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) active transporter, and dapagliflozin 3-O-glucuronide is a substrate for the OAT3 active transporter.
Dapagliflozin was not associated with clinically meaningful prolongation of QTc interval at daily doses up to 150 mg (15-times the recommended maximum dose) in a study of healthy subjects.

value.effect: The risk of hypoglycemia may be increased when FARXIGA is used concomitantly with insulin or insulin secretagogues.
value.management: Concomitant use may require lower doses of insulin or the insulin secretagogue to reduce the risk of hypoglycemia.

refs.quote: The risk of hypoglycemia may be increased when FARXIGA is used concomitantly with insulin or insulin secretagogues (e.g., sulfonylurea) [see Warnings and Precautions (5.4) ]. Intervention Concomitant use may require lower doses of insulin or the insulin secretagogue to reduce the risk of hypoglycemia.

value.effect: Concomitant use of an SGLT2 inhibitor with lithium may decrease serum lithium concentrations.
value.management: Monitor serum lithium concentration more frequently during FARXIGA initiation and dosage changes.

lactation_rid.value: No human breast milk data available

refs.quote: No quantitative human breast milk data are available for dapagliflozin. Summary of Use during Lactation: Because dapagliflozin passes into rat milk and causes renal tubular dilation during rodent kidney maturation (corresponding to human infancy), breastfeeding is not recommended during dapagliflozin therapy; prefer insulin or metformin.

lactation_summary.value: Transfers into animal milk with potential adverse effects on developing infant renal tubules; breastfeeding is not recommended (prefer insulin or metformin).

refs.locator: LactMed: dapagliflozin — Summary of Use during Lactation
refs.quote: Because dapagliflozin passes into rat milk and causes renal tubular dilation during rodent kidney maturation (corresponding to human infancy), breastfeeding is not recommended during dapagliflozin therapy; prefer insulin or metformin. [digoxin] Relative Infant Dose (RID): Breastfed infants receive approximately 1.9% to 4.1% of the weight

Since human kidney maturation occurs in utero and during the first 2 years of life when lactational exposure may occur, there may be risk to the developing human kidney. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants, advise women that use of FARXIGA is not recommended while breastfeeding.
